rationale: C05 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both proclamations follow the same distinctive sequence: identify a specific GATT schedule item and its existing concessionary duty; recite a Tariff Commission investigation finding increased imports and serious injury to a like or directly competitive domestic industry; cite section 350(a)(2); determine that modifying the concession and applying a revised duty is appropriate; then use paired paragraphs (a) and (b) to restate the schedule item and apply its modified rates, followed by a clause modifying the prior implementing proclamation. C02 is also a very close safeguard-duty precedent, but its paragraph (a) directly changes a quoted rate rather than using C05's closer 'item ... modified ... to read' formulation. C22 shares the injury-and-concession machinery but uses partial termination rather than the child's paired modification-and-application structure.

shared_material.parent_excerpt: the United States Tariff Commission has submitted to me its report of investigation and hearing under section 7 ... [and] has found that dried figs ... [are] being imported ... in such increased quantities ... as to cause serious injury to the domestic industry producing like or directly competitive products
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive parallel factual and administrative predicate for safeguard relief.
